newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN READY TO SIGN KLINSMANN FOR REST OF CAREER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN READY TO SIGN KLINSMANN FOR REST OF CAREER.

text.p: Bayern Munich are prepared to offer Juergen Klinsmann a contract for the rest of his playing career even though his scoring touch has vanished.

As second-placed Bayern prepare for a clash at middle-of- the-table Fortuna Duesseldorf on Saturday, it has emerged that the Bundesliga's richest club are ready to renew the Germany captain's contract when it ends in June 1998.
Klinsmann, 32, has lost his deadly finishing this season and missed several important chances in Bayern's 0-0 draw at home with reigning champions Borussia Dortmund last Sunday.
But former Germany skipper Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who is now Bayern vice-chairman, described the former Tottenham Hotspur player as a "guarantee for goals".
"We are interested in him staying until 1998 at the least. We could imagine Juergen staying longer," he said.
Klinsmann has been angered by the way some people have reacted to his problems this season. But Rummenigge said: "He knows he can rely on us."
The forward added: "Of course I am pleased when the club says something like that. I am always ready to listen to Bayern."

Klinsmann needs a goal at Fortuna to boost his confidence. After last weekend's two top-of-the-table clashes, this is a Friday and Saturday when most of the leading clubs must pick up points against less glamorous opposition.

Leaders VfB Stuttgart, ahead of Bayern on goal difference, play out-of-form Borussia Moenchengladbach at home on Saturday while fourth-placed Dortmund host bottom club Arminia Bielefeld, the same day.
Third-placed Bayer Leverkusen have a tougher task at fifth-placed Werder Bremen on Friday.

Bayern are still without leading Euro 96 players Thomas Helmer and Christian Ziege who both have long-term injuries. They must wait to see if midfielders Mario Basler and Thomas Strunz have recovered from less serious problems.
Basler had a superb game against Dortmund and the Bavarians need his influence in midfield.
Fortuna should be there for the taking. They have won just one of their five games at home this season. Last weekend they could only manage a goalless draw at struggling Duisburg.
